card.name: Sirtaki
card.tagline: The 1964 'Zorba's Dance' - Greece's famous invented dance.
card.profile: A 20th-century choreographed dance created for the 1964 film 'Zorba the Greek.' Mikis Theodorakis's 'Zorba's Dance' adapted a traditional Chania syrtos tune by composer Giorgis Koutsourelis; the film choreography is attributed to Giorgos Provias. It is NOT a traditional folk dance but an amalgam of slow hasapiko and faster hasaposerviko, with syrtos (dragging) and pidikhtos (hopping) elements. Danced in line or circle, hands on neighbours' shoulders; meter 4/4 accelerating, often shifting to 2/4 in the fast part, beginning slow then becoming vigorous with hops and leaps. Bouzouki-led music; performed at tavernas, weddings and festivals (English Wikipedia; Society of Folk Dance Historians).
card.insight: Despite global fame as 'Greek,' sirtaki is an invented tradition created for cinema; Anthony Quinn had a broken foot during filming, and the dragging-sliding steps replaced the planned hopping steps because he could not perform the dances taught to him (English Wikipedia).
